list.title: Are pimple patches effective?
list.content: Hydrocolloid Acne Pimple Patches are a form of spot treatment that works on existing pimples. It is a better alternative than popping your pimples, as these patches don't leave behind scars.

list.title: When should I apply a pimple patch?
list.content: Hydrocolloid Acne Pimple Patches should be used on inflamed acne skin or when you see a pimple showing white or yellow head.

list.title: Can I use pimple patch everyday?
list.content: You can use these patches if you have acne/pimples. They are safe for everyday and all day use.

list.title: Do pimple patches work on popped pimples?
list.content: Yes. If you put a patch over a popped pimple, it will collect the draining pus preventing further infection.

list.title: Can I shower with pimple patch?
list.content: Be Bodywise Hydrocolloid Acne Pimple Patches are water-proof. While it can be used during bathing, we'd recommend removing the patch while washing your face.

list.title: Do pimple patches leave scars?
list.content: Open and popped pimples often leave behind scars. Applying our Hydrocolloid Acne Pimple Patches helps cover up the affected area, preventing picking your acne - thus preventing scarring.

list.title: What is the white stuff on hydrocolloid patches?
list.content: The patch absorbs fluid from the wound, forming a white-gel like substance turning it white. This helps speed up healing and is completely safe for your skin.

list.title: How long can you wear hydrocolloid patches?
list.content: Although the pimples can subside within 48 hours, Be Bodywise Hydrocolloid Acne Pimple Patches are water-proof and make-up friendly and can be worn at a stretch of 3-5 days.

list.title: Does hydrocolloid work on blackheads?
list.content: Be Bodywise Hydrocolloid Acne Pimple Patches work only on surfaced acne and whiteheads. We wouldn't recommend using them for blackheads.

list.title: Can you put a pimple patch on an ingrown hair?
list.content: Be Bodywise Hydrocolloid Acne Pimple Patches work only on surfaced acne and whiteheads. It won't work on ingrown hair.

list.title: What are the side effects of hydrocolloid?
list.content: If you use the patches as instructed and in the areas suggested, it won't cause any side effects.

list.title: Can pimple patches remove blackheads?
list.content: Be Bodywise Hydrocolloid Acne Pimple Patches work only on surfaced acne and whiteheads. We wouldn't recommend using them for blackheads.

list.title: Can you sleep with pimple patches?
list.content: Yes, you can sleep after applying Be Bodywise Hydrocolloid Acne Pimple Patches. The strong adhesive won't come off letting your skin heal overnight.

list.title: Why do hydrocolloid patches turn white?
list.content: The patch absorbs fluid from the wound, forming a white-gel like substance turning it white. This helps speed up healing and is completely safe for your skin.

list.title: Do hydrocolloid patches work on blind pimples?
list.content: Be Bodywise Hydrocolloid Acne Pimple Patches work only on surfaced acne and whiteheads. It won't work on ingrown hair.

list.title: How to Use Acne Pimple Patch?
list.content: Here’s how to use an acne pimple patch by Be Bodywise-  Step 1: On cleansed face, cover the active acne with one patch of a suitable size. Step 2: Keep it overnight or a minimum for 6-8 hours and then remove it. Step 3: Repeat the procedure until the acne is completely dry.

list.title: What is Acne Patch?
list.content: An acne patch, also known as a pimple patch or acne sticker, is a small, adhesive patch that is designed to be placed directly on top of a pimple. These patches are typically made of hydrocolloid, a gel-like substance capable of absorbing excess oil and pus from pimples. Acne patches are frequently used as a spot treatment for pimples, especially those that have already popped. They can be worn under makeup and throughout the day, making them a convenient and discreet way to treat pimples.

list.title: Should I Pop Pimple Before Pimple Patch?
list.content: No, It is not recommended to pop a pimple before using a pimple patch. Popping a pimple can increase the risk of infection, inflammation, and scarring and can also make it more difficult for the pimple patch to adhere to the skin.
